newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court broadens application of Convention on judgments.
newsitem.headline: Court broadens application of Convention on judgments.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Thursday the Brussels Convention governing jurisdiction and the enforcement of judgments between member states may be raised to vacate a judgment for inadequate service of process even where the judgment was not issued as a result of default.

The Convention does not allow one member state to review the substantive reasoning another member state applied to reach a decision. However, the European court said "where proceedings are initiated against a person without his knowledge and a lawyer appears before the court first seised on his behalf but without his authority, such a person is quite powerless to defend himself."

According to the defendants based in the Netherlands, purchases were made without their knowledge or authority. When those purchases went unpaid, lawyers were engaged by the same unauthorized persons to appear in the name of the defendants, in Germany.
In such a context, the court said those persons must be regarded as defendants in default of appearance within the meaning of the Convention.

A member state court is not required, under Convention article 27(2), to recognize or enforce a default judgment issued in another member state if a defendant is not properly served with appropriate documents and with enough time to prepare his defence.

"The proper time for a defendant to have an opportunity to defend himself is the time at which proceedings are commenced. The possibility of having recourse, at a later stage, to a legal remedy against a judgment given in default of appearance, which has already become enforceable, cannot constititue an equally effective alternative to defending proceedings before judgment," the court said.
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: Dutch)
"Brussels Convention - Interpretation of article 27(2) - Recognition of a decision - Definition of a defendant in default of appearance"
Reference from the Hoge Raad der Nederlanden for a preliminary ruling in the proceedings pending before that court between

on the interpretation of article 27(1) and (2) and article 29 of the Convention of 27 September 1968 on jurisdiction and the enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters (OJ 1972 L 299, p. 32), as amended by the Convention of 9 October 1978 relating to the accession of the Kingdom of Denmark, Ireland and the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland (OJ 1978 L 304, p. 1 and, for the amended text, p. 77)

Article 27(2) of the Convention on of 27 September 1968 on jurisdiction and the enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters (OJ 1972 L 299, p. 32), as amended by the Convention of 9 October 1978 relating to the accession of the Kingdom of Denmark, Ireland and the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, applies to judgments given against a defendant who was not duly served with, or notified of, the document insitituting proceedings in sufficient time and who was not validly represented during those proceedings, albeit the judgments given were not given in default of appearance because someone puporting to represent the defendant appeared before the court first seised.
